note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: On ONE complete flowering culm, follow each branch from its attachment on the main axis. Dallisgrass is a coarse perennial with spreading to drooping racemes and paired overlapping spikelets in rows on the underside. Existing panel 0 teaches the branching habit but overlapping plants prevent a reliable total count. Branch count alone does NOT separate vaseygrass. New exact photographic reproductive views in gallery panels 7–9 (indices6–8) show attached rows and 5-mm scale, but still cannot establish total racemes on one full flowering head; whole flowering culm remains priority. Do not count several separate overlapping plants as one head.
tiles.status: VISIBLE HEAD; WHOLE SAME-PLANT PANICLE GAP

tiles.heading: 02 · FOLLOW THE ROOTED TUFT
tiles.details: Published Williamson County plants have a fibrous-rooted perennial tuft and short rhizomes with nodal roots; basal sheaths can be hairy. A complete same-plant root-to-head photograph with centimeter scale is missing. Do not infer underground rhizomes from the existing detached flowering-head panels.
tiles.short: Perennial clump with short rhizomes, not long stolons
tiles.status: PUBLISHED GROWTH FORM; ROOTED CROWN PHOTO GAP

tiles.heading: 03 · OPEN THE TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: Open the INNER blade–sheath junction. The Williamson County treatment describes a translucent membranous ligule about 2–5.5 mm; broader GrassBase accounts allow 2–8 mm. The physically archived Stefan.lefnaer source-identified CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph in gallery panel 5 (index 4) now visibly shows a translucent ligule flap, adjacent fine collar hairs and the photographer's 10-mm reference; three gross-structure arrows were separately pixel-reviewed. This is genuine anatomy evidence, but the free apex and exact membrane length were NOT independently measured, and the specimen is Croatian, not a Hays voucher. Joey panels 2–3 (indices 1–2) show external collar context only; never measure those hairs as the membrane.
tiles.short: Membranous ligule 2–5.5 mm in local treatment
tiles.status: TRUE LIGULE FLAP PHOTOGRAPHED — CALIBRATED FREE APEX AND LOCAL VOUCHER MISSING

tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE MATURE SPIKELETS
tiles.details: Find five ripe spikelets on one one-sided raceme and photograph flat and convex faces beside a physical 1-mm ruler at 10–20×. Williamson County reports upper glumes about 3.5–3.7 × 2.2–2.4 mm; broader GrassBase spikelet range is about 2.7–3.9 mm. Physically archived Harry Rose gallery panel 6 (index 5) visibly demonstrates oval attached spikelets and silky marginal hairs, with two pixel-reviewed gross arrows. It has NO calibrated ruler, so neither exact length nor a particular glume/lemma boundary is established. NEW Stefan CC BY-SA4 panels 7–9 now give actual 5-mm scale with enlarged attached oval spikelets, and an eight-faced view; distinctive pale marginal hairs are genuinely pictured. Still not separately isolated upper glume / lower sterile lemma or definite 3.5–3.7 mm individual measurement unless scale is calibrated in same plane.
tiles.short: Typically 3–4 mm; paired and broadly ovate
tiles.status: TRUE SILKY SPIKELETS PHOTOGRAPHED — MATURE MILLIMETER MEASUREMENT MISSING

tiles.heading: 05 · FIND THE SILKY UPPER GLUME
tiles.details: A true LOWER GLUME is absent. In the Williamson County treatment, the upper glume is spikelet-length, about 3.5–3.7 mm and 5–7-veined (broader treatments 3–9); the lower sterile lemma is near glume-length and the hard glossy upper fertile lemma about 2.2 mm locally (2–3.2 mm broadly). There is no long lemma awn: silky marginal glume hairs are not awns. Gallery panel 6 (index 5) now actually resolves silky hairs along attached oval spikelets, but does NOT distinguish their origin on the upper glume from overlapping bract edges. A ripe, forceps-separated and scaled spikelet is still required before glume, lemma, palea or vein arrows. NEW photos 7–9 visually establish true silky marginal hairs, some dark feathery STIGMAS (not awns) and close oval spikelet shape. Vaseygrass OTHER species gallery panel 10 has its photographer's own accurate glume/lemma labels; they CANNOT be re-used to prove Dallisgrass dissection. Actual upper glume/sterile lemma origin still needs dedicated dissection.
tiles.short: Lower glume absent; upper glume silky-edged; awnless
tiles.status: SILKY MARGINS VISIBLE — GLUME/LEMMA ORIGIN AND VEINS NEED DISSECTION

tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE VASEYGRASS
tiles.details: Paspalum urvillei commonly has more slender racemes (often 10–20) and smaller ripe spikelets (~2–3 mm), but head counts and spikelet sizes can overlap. Panel 3 is explicitly a DIFFERENT-SPECIES vaseygrass reference, not a Dallisgrass image. Compare equally mature, ruler-scaled spikelets, upper-glume hair placement, and a whole head from each species; avoid using wet habitat or clump size alone. NEW comparison panel 10 (index9) is a true locally archived vaseygrass original annotated glume/lemma; panel 11 (index10) is a true source-authenticated native Florida paspalum head with two branches. Both clearly labelled different species. Do not copy their organ labels to Dallisgrass and do not infer Florida paspalum Hays BONAP nativity status from non-Hays imagery.
tiles.short: Dallisgrass usually fewer racemes and larger silky spikelets
tiles.status: TWO VERIFIED VASEY/NATIVE FLORIDA PHOTO COMPARISONS NOW INCLUDED — SAME-SCALE SPIKELET DETAILS STILL OPEN

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: DALLISGRASS: on ONE complete seedhead count about 3–7(11) laterally spreading one-sided racemes. Its mature spikelets are generally 3–4 mm, broadly ovate and conspicuously LONG-SILKY-HAIRED at the upper-glume margins. Compare with vaseygrass: often 10–20 racemes and smaller 2–3 mm spikelets; these counts overlap. Existing Joey photos show the true racemes and leaf collar area, NOT measured ligules or the decisive silky margins.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: NEW REAL ANATOMY: source-author photos in gallery panels 7–9 (indices 6–8) show actual 5mm scale and three sets of hairy green oval attached spikelets in front/reverse. The dark feathery tufts are true flower stigmas, NOT awns; source photos do not individually assign upper glume/lemma.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Open the INNER blade–sheath junction. The Williamson County treatment describes a translucent membranous ligule about 2–5.5 mm; broader GrassBase accounts allow 2–8 mm. The physically archived Stefan.lefnaer source-identified CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph in gallery panel 5 (index 4) now visibly shows a translucent ligule flap, adjacent fine collar hairs and the photographer's 10-mm reference; three gross-structure arrows were separately pixel-reviewed. This is genuine anatomy evidence, but the free apex and exact membrane length were NOT independently measured, and the specimen is Croatian, not a Hays voucher. Joey panels 2–3 (indices 1–2) show external collar context only; never measure those hairs as the membrane.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Find five ripe spikelets on one one-sided raceme and photograph flat and convex faces beside a physical 1-mm ruler at 10–20×. Williamson County reports upper glumes about 3.5–3.7 × 2.2–2.4 mm; broader GrassBase spikelet range is about 2.7–3.9 mm. Physically archived Harry Rose gallery panel 6 (index 5) visibly demonstrates oval attached spikelets and silky marginal hairs, with two pixel-reviewed gross arrows. It has NO calibrated ruler, so neither exact length nor a particular glume/lemma boundary is established. NEW Stefan CC BY-SA4 panels 7–9 now give actual 5-mm scale with enlarged attached oval spikelets, and an eight-faced view; distinctive pale marginal hairs are genuinely pictured. Still not separately isolated upper glume / lower sterile lemma or definite 3.5–3.7 mm individual measurement unless scale is calibrated in same plane.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Measure 5 mature spikelets from the same head at 10–20×, showing edges backlit against a 1-mm ruler. Counts/height overlap P. urvillei. Paired spikelets are on a one-sided raceme, not awns. The pale hair tuft near blade/sheath in the Joey photo must not be labelled as a measured membranous ligule.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

intro: DALLISGRASS: on ONE complete seedhead count about 3–7(11) laterally spreading one-sided racemes. Its mature spikelets are generally 3–4 mm, broadly ovate and conspicuously LONG-SILKY-HAIRED at the upper-glume margins. Compare with vaseygrass: often 10–20 racemes and smaller 2–3 mm spikelets; these counts overlap. Existing Joey photos show the true racemes and leaf collar area, NOT measured ligules or the decisive silky margins.
memory_rule: COUNT COMPLETE RACEMES → MEASURE 5 RIPE SPIKELETS → CHECK MARGINAL HAIRS → ROOTED BASE/COLLAR. DALLIS few large silky; VASEY many small silky; FLORIDA few big round; PUBIFLORUM smaller oval; SETACEUM narrow variable; DISTICHUM two + real stolons.
safety_note: 8 actual same-species JPEGs physically hosted (three earlier Joey conditional CC BY-NC + five Commons CC BY/CC BY-SA), plus two other-species locally archived gallery panels P. urvillei and P. floridanum; existing earlier vaseygrass head makes 11 total gallery panels with THREE different-species comparisons. Actual two source-reproduced 5mm reproductive macros and one 8-angle plate now verified. True separated glume vs lemma, attached rooted whole perennial and fully countable intact head remain missing. The Joey photos' individually NC license version remains unverified. Live Pages and mobile QA separate.
field_rule: Dallisgrass usually 3–7 racemes with larger silky-margined spikelets, while vaseygrass commonly 10–20 racemes and smaller roughly 2–3 mm spikelets; counts overlap. Florida paspalum generally has fewer long branches and broad large oval spikelets. Bahia grass generally has two terminal racemes and lacks the distinct long marginal silky fringe characteristic of dallisgrass.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
comparison_text: Measure 5 mature spikelets from the same head at 10–20×, showing edges backlit against a 1-mm ruler. Counts/height overlap P. urvillei. Paired spikelets are on a one-sided raceme, not awns. The pale hair tuft near blade/sheath in the Joey photo must not be labelled as a measured membranous ligule.
